To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the effects of stimuli are due partly to their time to food and partly to their time until the next conditioned reinforcers, and (b) the effects of the latter are due partly to a stimulus' time to food and the time to the following conditioned reinforcer.
the time to food is the primary determinant of the effects of stimuli on behavior, but that the time to the conditioned reinforcer also has a substantial effect.
the effects of a conditioned reinforcer are due partly to time to food and partly to time to the next reinforcer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the temporal structure of schedules of reinforcement on the acquisition of behavior and with the effects of the temporal structure on the behavior maintained by reinforcement.
the effects of conditioned reinforcement in three-link concurrent chains.
the dynamics of the conditioned reinforcement process in a three-link concurrent-chain schedule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of the stimuli are due to the time to both food and to the next conditioned reinforcing stimulus in the sequence.
the time to food, and the time to the conditioned reinforcer, are the major factors that determine the effect of a conditioned stimulus in a chain schedule.
the conditioned reinforcement value of a stimulus depends on its association with a terminal link, and on the time to that terminal link.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

conditioned reinforcement dynamics are a function of the time to a conditioned reinforcer, the time to food, the nature of the conditioned reinforcer, and the stimuli associated with the conditioned reinforcer.

the time to the conditioned reinforcer is a more important factor than the time to food, and the time to food is a more important determinant of behavior than the time to the unconditioned reinforcer.

, in the case of concurrent chains, the time to the terminal link, the time to food, the time to a conditioned reinforcer, and the time to a stimulus associated with a conditioned reinforcer all contribute to preference for a given choice alternative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time to the subsequent conditioned reinforcer in a chain schedule has effects that are not predicted by the time to food.
conditioned reinforcement dynamics in a three-link concurrent chains schedule are not simply the sum of the effects of each link.

the effects of conditioned reinforcement in a chain schedule can be separated into two components: (1) the value of the conditioned reinforcement itself, which can be measured in terms of the time to the occurrence of a primary reinforcer; and (2) the value of a stimulus as a predictor of the occurrence of the next conditioned reinforcers.
